mainTopic: אונאה (overcharging) in a sale: the seller's rights when he is underpaid, and how long a buyer has to claim when the gap is less than a שתות (one-sixth).
overview: This amud finishes a ברייתא about אונאה: when an item worth six is sold for five, the seller was cheated, so he chooses to take back his item or collect the missing money. The גמרא then asks about the רבנן's time limit. When the gap is less than a שתות, is it forgiven right away, or only after enough time to show the item to a תגר or relative? It adds a side question: if both gaps get the same waiting time, what makes a שתות different? The answer is that a שתות lets the cheated person cancel the sale, while less than a שתות only brings a refund. The גמרא then goes back to the main question and tries to prove it from the משנה's story of the merchants of לוד, who returned to the words of the חכמים. The proof assumes that less than a third for רבי טרפון works like less than a sixth for the רבנן. If the small gap gets a waiting time, the merchants' choice makes sense, because רבי טרפון gave buyers the whole day. The גמרא starts testing the other option, that the small gap is forgiven immediately, and that thought continues on the next amud.

steps.title: When the seller is underpaid, he has the upper hand
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא finishes: if an item worth six was sold for five, the seller was cheated, so he may choose to take back his item or demand the missing money.
steps.simpleTranslation: If something worth six was sold for five, who was cheated? The seller. So the seller has the upper hand. If he wants, he says: 'Give me back my item,' or 'Give me the amount you cheated me.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes its rule for the case where the seller, not the buyer, was the one cheated.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The item was worth six but was sold for only five, so the seller lost out. Because he is the victim, the choice is his: he can cancel the sale and get his item back, or keep the sale going and collect the difference.

keyTerms.meaning: his hand is on top; he has the upper hand and gets to choose

phrases.english: An item worth six, sold for five,
who was cheated? The seller.
The seller has the upper hand.
If he wants, he says to him: 'Give me back my merchandise,'
or: 'Give me what you cheated me out of.'

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁוֶה שֵׁשׁ בְּחָמֵשׁ, מִי נִתְאַנָּה – מוֹכֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes a ברייתא that began before this section, applying its rule to the seller's side.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the seller is underpaid by a שתות, he chooses between cancelling the sale and collecting the difference.

steps.title: Is a gap of less than a sixth forgiven right away?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: according to the רבנן, when the gap is less than a שתות, is it forgiven immediately, or only after the time it takes to show the item to a merchant or relative?
steps.simpleTranslation: A question was asked: according to the רבנן, when the gap is less than a sixth, is it forgiven right away, or only after enough time to show the item to a merchant or a relative?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new question about timing, meaning the moment a small gap counts as forgiven.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן give a buyer only as long as it takes to show the item to a תגר or relative to make an אונאה claim. The question is whether that same waiting period also applies to a gap smaller than a שתות, or whether such a small gap counts as מחילה (forgiven) from the very first moment.

keyTerms.meaning: a question was asked before them (the חכמים)

phrases.english: A question was asked before them:
When the gap is less than a sixth, according to the Rabbis,
is it forgiven immediately,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ בִּכְדֵי שֶׁיַּרְאֶה לַתַּגָּר אוֹ לִקְרוֹבוֹ?
phrases.english: or only after the time it takes to show it to a merchant or to his relative?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: the timing of מחילה under the רבנן.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: At what moment a gap of less than a שתות counts as forgiven: immediately, or after the time needed to show the item.

steps.title: Then what is the difference between a sixth and less?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא adds a side question: if less than a שתות also gets the waiting time, how is it different from a gap of exactly a שתות?
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say it also gets the time to show a merchant or relative, then what is the difference between a gap of a sixth and a gap of less than a sixth?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up a side question that would come up if the second side of the question turns out to be right.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If both kinds of gap share the same time limit, they might seem to be the same law. The גמרא wants to know what would still set them apart.

keyTerms.meaning: and if you will say (a side question built on one possible answer)

phrases.english: And if you will say
that it is only after the time it takes to show it to a merchant or to his relative,

phrases.aramaic: מַאי אִיכָּא בֵּין שְׁתוּת לְפָחוֹת מִשְּׁתוּת?
phrases.english: what difference is there between a sixth and less than a sixth?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the second side of the question in step 2.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What would still set a שתות apart from less than a שתות if both share the same time limit.
steps.confusionAlert: This is not a second, separate question that needs its own proof. It only asks what the difference would be if the second option of step 2 is correct, and it gets answered right away in the next step.

steps.title: A sixth lets you cancel; less than a sixth only gets a refund
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that there is a difference. With a שתות, the cheated person can cancel the sale or keep it and get a refund. With less than a שתות, the sale stands and only the overcharge is returned.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a difference. With a sixth, he has the upper hand: if he wants, he cancels; if he wants, he keeps the purchase and the overcharge is returned. With less than a sixth, the purchase stands and the overcharge is returned.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the side question from step 3 by showing that the two cases still differ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if both cases share the same time limit, the cheated person's options are not the same. A gap of a שתות gives him a choice that includes cancelling. A gap of less than a שתות never cancels the sale; it only brings a refund of the אונאה.

phrases.english: There is a difference: with a sixth,
he has the upper hand:
if he wants, he backs out;
if he wants, he keeps the purchase and the overcharge is returned.
Whereas with less than a sixth,
the purchase stands, and the overcharge is returned.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the side question of step 3.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A שתות gives the option to cancel or keep the sale with a refund. Less than a שתות means the sale stands with only a refund.
steps.whatToRemember: The side question is settled: a שתות allows cancelling, and less than a שתות only brings a refund. The main timing question from step 2 has not been answered yet; the next step goes back to it with a proof from the משנה.

steps.title: Trying to answer from the merchants of לוד
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to the main question and begins a proof from the משנה's line that the merchants of לוד went back to the words of the חכמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: So what is the answer? Come and hear: 'They went back to the words of the Sages.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the open question from step 2 and starts bringing a proof from the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי טרפון gave buyers more time to back out, and the merchants of לוד asked to go back to the earlier rule. The גמרא is about to show what this ending teaches about when a gap of less than a שתות is forgiven.

keyTerms.meaning: they went back to the words of the Sages

phrases.english: What is the answer? Come and hear:
They went back to the words of the Sages.
phrases.notes: This is the end of the משנה's story about רבי טרפון and the merchants of לוד.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי? תָּא שְׁמַע: חָזְרוּ לְדִבְרֵי חֲכָמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the side question behind and returns to the main question of step 2.
steps.raayaObject: The timing of מחילה for a gap of less than a שתות under the רבנן.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's ending: the merchants of לוד went back to the words of the חכמים.

steps.title: The assumption behind the proof
steps.stepSummary: The proof assumes that 'less than a third' for רבי טרפון follows the same rule as 'less than a sixth' for the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: They assumed that less than a third according to רבי טרפון is like less than a sixth according to the רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא lays down the starting assumption its proof will build on. It is setting up the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each opinion has a cutoff: a third for רבי טרפון and a sixth for the רבנן. The assumption is that the zone just below each cutoff follows the same timing rule. Whatever happens to 'less than a sixth' for the רבנן also happens to 'less than a third' for רבי טרפון.

keyTerms.meaning: They assumed (the people thinking through the proof)
Less than a third, the gap below רבי טרפון's cutoff
Is like, is the same as

phrases.english: They assumed: less than a third according to Rabbi Tarfon
is like less than a sixth according to the Rabbis.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the hidden assumption behind the proof that was opened in step 5.
steps.raayaObject: Whether less than a שתות is forgiven right away or only after the waiting time, according to the רבנן.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's report that the merchants of לוד went back to the words of the חכמים.

steps.title: If there is a waiting time, the merchants' choice makes sense
steps.stepSummary: If less than a sixth gets a waiting time under the רבנן, while רבי טרפון gives a whole day, the merchants had a good reason to go back to the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: It works well if you say that for less than a sixth, the רבנן give only the time it takes to show the item to a merchant or relative, while רבי טרפון gives the whole day. That is why the merchants went back.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that one side of the question explains the משנה well: the merchants went back because the רבנן gave a shorter time to claim the refund.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under רבי טרפון the merchants gained a bigger allowed margin, but buyers could claim refunds all day. Under the רבנן, the gap below the cutoff could only be claimed for a short time. So going back to the רבנן gave the merchants a real benefit.

keyTerms.meaning: It works well if you say, this side fits nicely
A merchant, someone who knows prices

phrases.english: It works well if you say
that less than a sixth according to the Rabbis
is claimable for the time it takes to show it to a merchant or his relative,
and according to Rabbi Tarfon, the whole day,
that is why they went back.
phrases.notes: 'They' are the merchants of לוד from the משנה, who went back to the words of the חכמים.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the assumption from step 6 to show that the 'waiting time' side fits the משנה.
steps.raayaObject: Supports the view that less than a שתות gets the waiting time under the רבנן.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The merchants of לוד going back to the חכמים.

steps.title: Setting up the other side: forgiven immediately
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins to test the other side: what if less than a sixth is forgiven right away under the רבנן?
steps.simpleTranslation: But if you say that for less than a sixth according to the רבנן, it is forgiven immediately,
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts the opposite option to show it will not fit the משנה. The sentence continues on the next amud, where the problem with this option is spelled out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אלא signals a turn to the other side of the question. On this side, the buyer forgives the small overcharge on the spot, with no waiting time at all. The גמרא is preparing to show that this would not explain why the merchants went back.

keyTerms.meaning: But, turning to the other option

steps.confusionAlert: This is not the end of the thought. The גמרא has only stated the option here; the reason it fails comes right after.

phrases.english: But if you say
that less than a sixth according to the Rabbis
is forgiven immediately,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the side that fits (step 7) to the side the proof will reject.
steps.raayaObject: Testing the option that less than a שתות is forgiven right away under the רבנן.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The merchants of לוד going back to the חכמים.
